Name: workflow-escalate-to-human
Description__c: Escalation workflow for unresolved issues or explicit handoff requests.
WhenToUse__c: Use when troubleshooting does not resolve issue, user requests human, or policy requires escalation.
InstructionBody__c:
# ESCALATE TO A HUMAN

## When to escalate
Escalate only if either:
- the customer explicitly asks for a human, an agent, or escalation; or
- you walked them through the troubleshooting steps in this conversation, the issue is still unresolved, and they agree to escalate.

If they want to keep troubleshooting, keep troubleshooting. Frustration, repeated questions, out-of-scope topics (billing disputes, legal, safety, VIP), and policy requests (refunds, complaints) are reasons to offer escalation, never to escalate without asking.

## Steps
### 1. Confirm
Ask the customer to confirm they want to be handed to a human before you use any escalation tool.

### 2. Set expectations
Tell the customer you are connecting them, that a specialist will join shortly, and that you will share the conversation so they do not have to repeat themselves.

### 3. Prepare the handoff
Write a three-to-five-sentence summary covering the issue, what was tried, the escalation reason, and the customer's sentiment.

### 4. Hand off
- Open the handoff ticket with [[tool:CreateEscalationTicket]] once you have the customer ID, a one-sentence issue description, and an issue type (technical, billing, or general).
- Route the customer to a human with [[tool:Route_to_ESA]].

### 5. Close the loop
Share the ticket reference and confirm that the specialist will have the full context.

Name: workflow-support-case-lifecycle
WhenToUse__c: Use when opening, updating, or closing customer support cases.
InstructionBody__c:
# SUPPORT CASE LIFECYCLE

## Steps
### 1. Verify identity
Follow core-skill-user-otp-authentication and send the code with [[tool:SendVerificationEmail]]. Do not continue until verification succeeds.

### 2. Intake
Capture the issue in the customer's words, its severity (Critical, High, Medium, or Low), the business impact, and the case type (Technical, Billing, Replacement, Refund, or General).

### 3. Create or update
- To create, use [[tool:CreateCase]] with the summary the customer approved.
- To update, add progress notes and move the status from Open to In Progress to Completed.

### 4. Confirm
Share the case number, the expected time to the next update (for example 24 to 48 hours), and the agreed next steps.

### 5. Close
When the issue is resolved, set the case to Completed, confirm with the customer, and ask if they need anything else.

### 6. Escalate
If the customer asks for a human at any point, follow workflow-escalate-to-human.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-wifi-modem
WhenToUse__c: Use when user has internet outage, unstable Wi-Fi, or modem light issues.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: WI-FI MODEM

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the modem model, when the problem started, and the status of the Power, WAN, LAN, and Wi-Fi lights. Green means normal, amber means a problem, red means an error, and off means no power.

### 2. Power cycle
Unplug the modem and router and wait 60 seconds. Plug in the modem first and wait for its lights to settle, then plug in the router and wait 2 to 3 minutes. Test the connection.

### 3. Check cables
Confirm the coax or Ethernet cables are secure, the modem connects to the router's WAN port (not a LAN port), and try a different power outlet.

### 4. Check for an outage
Ask whether neighbors are affected and suggest checking the provider's outage map.

### 5. Escalate
If the problem persists after the power cycle and cable checks, or a red light stays on, follow workflow-escalate-to-human.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-5g-modem
Description__c: Troubleshoot 5G modem signal and throughput issues.
WhenToUse__c: Use when 5G modem has low signal or unstable service.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: 5G MODEM

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the modem model, whether it is indoors or outdoors, the signal strength (RSRP; values closer to zero are stronger), the firmware version, and any obstructions such as concrete or metal.

### 2. Improve placement
- Move the modem near a window with as few obstructions as possible, away from concrete, brick, and metal.
- Rotate it toward the nearest tower.
- Low-band signals penetrate walls best, mid-band balances range and speed, and mmWave needs a clear line of sight.

### 3. Refresh the modem
- Power cycle it: unplug for 60 seconds, then plug it back in.
- Update the firmware.
- Check that the SIM or eSIM is seated and active.

### 4. Escalate
If RSRP is below -100 dBm, SINR is below 10 dB, or throughput is still low after these steps, follow workflow-escalate-to-human.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-iphone-16
WhenToUse__c: Use for iPhone 16 configuration, connectivity, or app behavior support.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: IPHONE 16

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the iOS version (Settings > General > About), the affected feature (Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth, VPN, or an app), and when the problem started.

### 2. Basic checks
Confirm Wi-Fi is on and Airplane Mode is off, restart the phone, restart the router or modem, and turn off any VPN temporarily.

### 3. Reset network settings
If the problem persists, go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings, enter the passcode, and confirm. Then rejoin Wi-Fi and re-pair Bluetooth devices. Explain that this removes saved networks but does not affect photos or apps.

### 4. Escalate
If the problem persists, follow workflow-escalate-to-human.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-iphone-16-pro
WhenToUse__c: Use for iPhone 16 Pro technical issues.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: IPHONE 16 PRO

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the iOS version, the symptom (display stuck at 60 Hz, black camera, flashlight not working, or app crashes), and whether it can be reproduced.

### 2. Display stuck at 60 Hz
In Settings > Accessibility > Motion, turn off Limit Frame Rate and Reduce Motion. Then force restart: press Volume Up, press Volume Down, and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.

### 3. Camera and flashlight
Force restart, close other apps, and free up storage. If the problem persists, back up the phone and restore it with a computer.

### 4. General
Update iOS and reset network settings for connectivity problems.

### 5. Escalate
If a hardware defect remains after the software steps, follow workflow-escalate-to-human.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-galaxy-s25
Description__c: Troubleshoot Samsung Galaxy S25 device issues.
WhenToUse__c: Use for Galaxy S25 network, battery, and app-related issues.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: GALAXY S25

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the One UI version (Settings > About phone > Software information), any recent changes, and the symptom: network, battery, app crashes, or lag.

### 2. Network problems
Restart the phone, install software updates, reset network settings, turn off any VPN, and forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network.

### 3. Battery problems
- Set Motion smoothness from Adaptive to Standard (60 Hz).
- Restrict background apps and turn on Adaptive battery.
- For overheating, lower the brightness, turn off Always On Display, and avoid heavy use while charging.

### 4. Escalate
If the issue is unresolved, follow workflow-escalate-to-human. Suggest the Samsung Members app for sending an error report.

Name: workflow-troubleshooting-galaxy-s25-ultra
Description__c: Troubleshoot Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra device issues.
WhenToUse__c: Use for Galaxy S25 Ultra camera, connectivity, and performance issues.
InstructionBody__c:
# TROUBLESHOOTING: GALAXY S25 ULTRA

## Steps
### 1. Gather details
Ask for the symptom (camera quality, color or processing, display touch, or overheating), which camera app is used (stock, Expert Raw, or third-party), and the One UI version.

### 2. Camera
- The stock camera and Expert Raw apply AI processing; third-party apps may look different.
- Turn off AI enhancements in the camera settings if the customer prefers unprocessed photos.
- If the problem looks like hardware or persists, go to step 5.

### 3. Display and touch
Remove any screen protector, turn on Touch sensitivity in Display settings, lower the brightness, and turn off Always On Display.

### 4. Overheating
Turn on Adaptive battery, lower the brightness, and avoid heavy camera use while charging.

### 5. Escalate
If camera or display issues are unresolved, follow workflow-escalate-to-human. Suggest the Samsung Members app for expert support.
